title: Expected-Supremum Precision of the Functional ATT Curve at Every Visit Frequency
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered subfield below field floor: paper score ceiling 7.2 < field threshold 7.4, with no bounded in-scope tier lift; main all-visits minimax theorem sound but auxiliary time-only upper uniformization and Sant Anna-Zhao positioning remain incomplete.
gap_reasons: The delivered theorem proves a same-class polynomial minimax frontier, with both the localized interaction lower bound and the visit-insensitive scalar plateau matched by an observable estimator up to logarithmic factors.
It does not determine the exact expected-supremum minimax rate because the lower and upper logarithmic factors and their crossover remain open
The contribution is confined to a highly structured benchmark with known visit densities, uniform control covariates, balanced treatment prevalence, fixed dimension ten, and Lipschitz smoothness
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established an all-visits polynomial minimax bracket with sparse-visit and shared-intercept lower-bound branches, a block second-moment bound, and an observable robust estimator. The field-tier claim stopped at D0.5 because the exact expected-supremum logarithmic frontier remained open and the structured benchmark capped the paper score at 7.2, below the 7.4 field threshold. The auxiliary time-only upper uniformization and a Sant'Anna-Zhao comparison sentence remain incomplete; the headline theorem is sound and the achieved tier is subfield.
tldr: The note determines the polynomial expected-supremum precision of the identified functional ATT curve for every visit frequency.  An exact fixed-\(n\) localized mixture gives the interaction obstruction \((n^2m)^{-2/15}\), while a new time-constant shared-random-intercept branch has Gaussian information \(m/(\sigma^2+mv_0)\), uniformly bounded in \(m\), and proves the same-class scalar floor \(n^{-2/7}\).  The finite observable multiresolution estimator matches the resulting frontier \(\max\{(n^2m)^{-2/15},n^{-2/7}\}\) up to logarithms.  The polynomial exponent is \((4+2\rho)/15\) for \(m\asymp n^\rho\) up to \(\rho=1/7\) and plateaus at \(2/7\) thereafter.  The block second-moment lemma is proved; only the exact logarithmic frontier remains open.
gap: Functional DiD theory supplies identification and first-order inference after sufficiently accurate curve reconstruction, random-visit mean theory supplies noncausal sampling transitions, and causal higher-order theory supplies scalar nuisance-product rates. None of the inspected theorem statements combines one static density channel, one time-localized regression channel, exactly \(n\) independent subjects, and whole-curve expected supremum loss.
fill: The project pairs an exact multinomial fixed-sample mixture lower bound with an observable split-sample dyadic estimator whose geometric time bandwidths control quadratic variance using only groupwise pointwise moments.
